ProgramName: Master of Science in Marketing
Requirements: The application process for the Master of Science in Marketing program consists of three steps: an online application, submission of transcripts and test scores, and a video assessment. [2] The admissions committee looks for applicants with scholastic aptitude, strong communication skills, and a demonstrated interest in marketing. [12] While there is no specific undergraduate major required, an indication of mathematical ability through coursework is considered. Description: Texas McCombs' Master of Science in Marketing (MSM) is a 10-month, STEM-eligible master's degree program that combines a traditional marketing education with cutting-edge data analytics training. Grounded in applied marketing analytics, the MSM program prepares students for a marketing career in a new economy where data, decisions, and creativity are intertwined. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in marketing principles combined with advanced data analytics training, equipping students to understand and leverage analytics in strategic decision-making. Graduates leave the program with the quantitative and qualitative skills to create transformative marketing strategies for companies across various industries.

[4] The program is designed to give students the expertise necessary to convert scientific knowledge and technology to wealth by creating new products, services, and ventures. [4] Students in the program study all aspects of starting and managing entrepreneurial and intrapreneurial ventures, assessing a technology's commercial potential, and accelerating the movement of products and services from conception to market introduction and growth. This graduate program offers training in seven different research tracks: Bioinformatics & Computational Biology. Cell & Developmental Biology. Chemical Biology & Drug Discovery. Molecular Genetics. Neurobiology. Biomolecular Structure and Function. Plant Molecular Biology. [4, 6] Each of the tracks provides specialized courses and training for the graduate student beyond the basic core curriculum of genetics, biochemistry, molecular biology, and cell biology. [6] The Interdisciplinary Life Sciences Graduate Programs, a research unit housed in the College of Natural Sciences, provides the support and infrastructure for the Cell and Molecular Biology (CMB) graduate program at The University of Texas at Austin. [6]
ScholarshipType: Graduate Research Assistantship, Teaching Assistantship, Fellowships

ProgramName: Artist Diploma in Music Performance
Requirements: Applying to The University of Texas at Austin as a graduate music major is a two-part process that requires separate applications to the University and the Sarah and Ernest Butler School of Music. The Artist Diploma is a highly specialized and performance-oriented non-degree graduate certificate program for exceptional musicians. To be considered for admission, applicants must meet the admission requirements for performance majors. The faculty use prescreening recordings to determine whether or not to invite an applicant for a live, on-campus audition. A list of all solo works that have been performed is also required, along with letters of recommendation.
Concentration: ['Instrumental Performance (e.g., Piano, Guitar, Tuba, Harp, Strings)', 'Opera Performance', 'Chamber Music']
Description: The two-year Artist Diploma (A.D.) in Music Performance is a highly specialized and performance-oriented non-degree graduate certificate program for exceptional musicians who have great potential for a professional career in music performance at the international level. [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9]

ProgramName: Advanced Practice Registered Nurse Certification
Requirements: The post-master's Advanced Practice Registered Nurse Certification (APRN) certificate programs are for nurses who hold a master's degree in nursing from an accredited program. To be eligible, applicants need to have completed an upper-division statistics course before the first semester. The program offers several tracks, including Acute Care Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Family Nurse Practitioner, Primary Care Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, and Adult-Gerontology Clinical Nurse Specialist, with a coursework requirement of 24 to 29 semester hours depending on the track.
Concentration: Acute Care Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Family Nurse Practitioner, Primary Care Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, or Adult-Gerontology Clinical Nurse Specialist
Description: The post-master's Advanced Practice Registered Nurse Certification (APRN) certificate programs are designed for those nurses who have a master's degree in nursing from a program accredited by the National League for Nursing or the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education or a recognized degree from a foreign academic institution and wish to complete the course work necessary to sit for national certification as an APRN. Students choose a certificate track as an Acute Care Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Family Nurse Practitioner, Primary Care Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, or Adult-Gerontology Clinical Nurse Specialist. Depending on the chosen track, students must complete a minimum of 24 to 29 semester hours of coursework.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Engineering Education
Requirements: The Graduate Certificate in Engineering Education is designed for graduate students interested in pursuing engineering faculty positions upon graduation. [2] To complete the certificate, students must finish 16 credits of specified coursework, including Teaching Engineering, Curriculum Design and Assessment in Engineering, an elective, a Teaching Practicum, and Teaching Portfolio Prep. [2] Students are required to complete the Graduate Certificate in Engineering Education Reporting Form and submit it to the Graduate School during the semester they are completing the requirements and graduating. [2]
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Engineering Education is designed for graduate students interested in pursuing engineering faculty positions upon graduation. [1] This certificate program will prepare students for the instructional aspects of a faculty career and increase their competitiveness for faculty jobs. [1] Courses are active, discussion-based and focused on applying research on learning to the engineering pedagogy. [1] Graduate students seeking this certificate will gain experience in teaching undergraduate engineering courses, learn more about research on teaching and learning, develop their own ideas and philosophy on teaching and create materials that will help in their faculty job search. [1]

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Latin American Architecture
Requirements: The stackable graduate certificate is open to any UT Austin degree-seeking graduate student and requires three classes (nine credit hours).
Concentration: Latin American Architecture
Description: The Stackable Graduate Certificate in Architecture: Latin American Architecture allows graduate students to develop a comparative approach to architectural education and scholarship. [1] By enhancing and promoting a regional focus that already exists in the school's graduate curriculum, the Stackable Graduate Certificate in Architecture: Latin American Architecture allows graduate students to develop a comparative approach to architectural education and scholarship. [1] It will also equip them with tools to engage in the effect that globalization has on architecture and place more broadly. As a result, program participants will not only become experts in Latin American Architecture, they will also become better equipped to address the world's most pressing issues regarding the built environment. [1] The stackable graduate certificate is open to any UT Austin degree-seeking graduate student and requires three classes (nine credit hours). [1]

ProgramName: Ad Hoc Interdisciplinary Doctoral Program
Requirements: The Ad Hoc Interdisciplinary Doctoral Program allows students who have already been admitted to an established doctoral program at the University of Texas at Austin to create a personalized course of study. [1, 4] Interested students should first consult with the graduate adviser of the program they are admitted to. [1, 3, 4] The student, in conjunction with their adviser and a proposed committee, will develop a program of work and dissertation topic. [1] Once an agreement is reached, the graduate adviser submits the 'Application for Ad Hoc Interdisciplinary Doctoral Program' form to the Graduate School for approval. [1] This form must contain a brief statement of the proposed interdisciplinary dissertation topic, a statement from the supervising faculty member, and a statement from the graduate adviser outlining the requirements for admission to candidacy. [1]
Description: Students admitted to established academic programs may propose to construct an ad hoc interdisciplinary doctoral program that draws on the intellectual resources of several graduate programs and involves faculty members from more than one college or school. [2] This procedure allows students who have been admitted to a graduate program to design a course of study that does not fit into an existing degree plan. [2] Each program must be approved by the graduate dean. [2] Students interested in the ad hoc interdisciplinary doctoral program should consult the graduate advisor of the program to which they are admitted or to which they plan to apply. [2]

ProgramName: Combined JD/PhD in government
Requirements: The program is a combined degree officially called the "Law and Government Program" (LGP), leading to a J.D. in law and a Ph.D. in Government. [9] Students are required to apply separately and secure admission to both the School of Law and the Department of Government. [9] By counting some law courses towards the Ph.D. and some Government courses towards the J.D., students can potentially reduce the time needed to earn both degrees. [9, 12] The admissions committee for the Government department considers the applicant's academic record, test scores (GRE, TOEFL/IELTS), Resume/CV, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, and writing sample. [7]
Department: School of Law and College of Liberal Arts, Department of Government

ProgramName: Combined JD/PhD in philosophy
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements for graduate study at the University of Texas, the following are required for admission to the graduate program in philosophy: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. An official transcript from every college and university attended. Three letters of recommendation from persons in a position to evaluate the applicant's academic ability and promise for graduate study. A statement of purpose of one to two pages describing the applicant's philosophical interests and goals. A sample of philosophical writing of no more than 20 pages. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission and will not be considered.
Description: The School of Law and the Graduate School offer programs leading to the Doctor of Jurisprudence and the Doctor of Philosophy with a major in government or philosophy. [4] These programs are designed to prepare students for academic careers in law or the cognate discipline or both. [4] By counting law courses toward the PhD and courses in the cognate discipline toward the JD, students can save up to a year of coursework. [4]
MinimumGreScore: Median for recent applicants is 329 (verbal + quantitative)

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in African and African diaspora studies
Requirements: To apply, interested UT-Austin doctoral students must submit a completed application form, a one-page description of their research project, a one-page personal statement explaining why the portfolio is important to their academic work, and their most recent Curriculum Vitae. [1] Students must be in good standing in an approved UT-Austin doctoral program, have the approval of their faculty advisor and department's Graduate Advisor, and maintain a GPA of 3.3 or better. [1, 4] The program requires the completion of 12 hours of graduate-level AFR coursework, including AFR 390 and AFR 391, and a research presentation to an open audience before graduation. [1]
Fees.1: $12,006 for in-state and $22,954 for out-of-state students
Concentration: ['Critical race theory', 'Black queer theory', 'Black political theory and economics', 'Black arts and performance studies', 'Black diaspora history and anthropology', 'Black feminisms']
Description: The objectives of the AADS Doctoral Portfolio program are to engage doctoral students in an advanced approach to interdisciplinary studies and to provide tools for mapping the intellectual, political, and creative breadth of African and African Diaspora Studies. [2] Students in the program participate in rigorous dialogue; expand the university's resources through the development of interdisciplinary methodologies; become familiar with the diverse faculty specialties within African and African Diaspora Studies; foster UT-Austin's national and international reputation as a recognized leader in African and African Diaspora Studies; and are instructed in the application of theoretical and conceptual tools of analysis and research on African-descended peoples. [2] The graduate program in AADS provides students with the skills and analytical frameworks necessary to engage interdisciplinary approaches for examining the lives of people of African descent throughout Africa and the African Diaspora, including the United States, the Caribbean, and Latin America. [3] AADS students interrogate understandings of Blackness and how it is expressed throughout the Diaspora, while engaging in subfields of critical race theory, Black queer theory, Black political theory and economics, Black arts and performance studies, Black diaspora history and anthropology, and Black feminisms. [3]
CostPerCredit: $659 for Texas residents and $1,245 for out-of-state students

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Aging and health
Description: An official credential appearing on the transcript, a portfolio program provides an organizing framework for students who wish to focus on a particular area of inquiry. Portfolio programs encourage students to build an intellectual community with peers and faculty from a variety of disciplines. Students in the portfolio program in Aging & Health must attend at least 4 lectures sponsored by the Aging Network OR participate in the Aging Network Graduate Council for at least 3 semesters. A written scholarly report must be presented to the Aging & Health adviser and be approved by the Aging & Health faculty, before the program is complete. For doctoral students, this report will typically be one chapter of the dissertation. For master’s students, the report may be the master’s thesis or a report from a master’s course.

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Arts and cultural management and entrepreneurship
Requirements: The Portfolio in Arts and Cultural Management and Entrepreneurship is open to all University of Texas students currently enrolled in a master's or doctoral level degree in good standing in their departments. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 and permission of their graduate adviser. [1]
Department: The Graduate Portfolio Program in Arts and Cultural Management and Entrepreneurship is jointly sponsored by the College of Fine Arts and the Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs. [5]
Description: The Portfolio in Arts and Cultural Management and Entrepreneurship is a certification program that provides students with cross-disciplinary theoretical and practical training related to the management arid governance of arts and cultural organizations, and/or the business dimensions of an entrepreneurial artistic career. [2] Further goals are to promote greater interaction among students, faculty, and others working in areas related to these fields; provide increased visibility and offerings in the field on campus, and; promote interaction between Austin's cultural community and UT-Austin students, faculty, and others with an interest in arts and cultural management and entrepreneurship. [2] The Portfolio is jointly sponsored by the College of Fine Arts and the Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs, and engages faculty from across the university. [2]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Asian American studies
Description: The Graduate Portfolio in Asian American Studies provides certification of teaching and research expertise for MA and Ph.D. students working on projects concerning Asian American and Asian Diaspora Studies. [1] The program serves students interested with questions of migration and citizenship, transnationalism and globalization, the politics of representation, race, ethnicity, gender, social theory, postcolonialism, neoliberalism, and imperialism. [1] Relevant courses are taught by faculty across campus, but particularly in the areas of media and communications, English, History, American Studies, Human Ecology, Education, Anthropology, Sociology, Social Work, comparative race and ethnicity, Women and Gender Studies, Asian Studies, and public policy. [1] The AAS portfolio is intended to complement existing programs and should not extend time to graduation. [1]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Communication, information, and cultural policy
Requirements: Each academic department determines its own policy regarding application requirements. [1]
Department: The Graduate Portfolio Program in Communication, Information, and Cultural Policy is an interdisciplinary program. Students from any participating school or college at the University of Texas at Austin may apply. The program is administratively housed in the School of Journalism and Media within the Moody College of Communication.
Description: The Graduate Portfolio in Communication, Information, and Cultural Policy offers students at the University of Texas a means to enter this vital field of study by focusing on the theory, history, and comparative aspects of policy. [2] The program supports students' preparation for careers in academic research or practical careers in policy-making arenas. [2] Study in Communication, Information, and Cultural Policy is well-suited to a portfolio certificate program because it is a multi-disciplinary subject that can find students drawing on public policy, economics, communications, art, community planning, and information science. [1, 2] This program invites students to integrate these disciplines into their particular course of study and provides an institutional home for scholars with these shared interests. [1, 2]
ScholarshipType: The University of Texas at Austin offers various forms of financial assistance to graduate students, including fellowships and scholarships. [6]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Computational medicine
Requirements: The Computational Medicine Portfolio Program is intended for graduate students with strong mathematical and physical science backgrounds, but limited knowledge of biology and/or medicine. [1] Students must apply and obtain approval from the Computational Medicine Portfolio Committee for their list of courses. [1] Student must have approval from their Graduate Advisor. [1] An application form is required. [1]
Department: Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Sciences

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Cultural studies
Requirements: Candidates must be students in good standing in an approved doctoral program and receive approval to enter the Portfolio Program from their Graduate Advisor. [2] The application requires the submission of the Cultural Studies Portfolio Application form, a statement of purpose, a letter of approval from the graduate advisor, and a sample Doctoral Portfolio program of work that lists courses and the rationale for their selection. [1]
Department: College of Liberal Arts, College of Communication, College of Fine Arts
Description: Graduate portfolio programs provide opportunities for enrolled graduate students to obtain transcriptable credentials in cross-disciplinary academic areas of inquiry while they are completing the requirements for a master's or doctoral degree in a particular discipline. [1] The Américo Paredes Center for Cultural Studies (APCCS) has a long history of fostering interdisciplinary approaches to the study of varied cultural forms and offers a doctoral portfolio in Cultural Studies. [2] Portfolio programs are intended to promote cross-disciplinary scholarship and study by bringing together faculty and students from a variety of disciplines whose interests transcend boundaries of traditional academic disciplines. [1] The program draws together students and faculty from various disciplines such as Literature, Radio-Television-Film, Ethnomusicology, and Theatre and Drama. [2]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Digital studies
Requirements: The application requires a brief statement of the student's interests in the program and their research goals, a rationale for pursuing this course of study, and a clear sense of how pursuing this course of study guides them towards particular graduate and career goals. Students must be in good academic standing to apply (with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above). [1] Graduate students, including those from departments with no faculty representatives in the program, can enter the portfolio program at any point in their graduate work. [1]
Description: Scholarship in Digital Studies interprets the cultural and social impact of new media and information technologies as well as creates and applies these technologies to answer cultural, social, historical, and philological questions. [1] Digital Studies is necessarily collaborative and interdisciplinary. [1] It emphasizes design, multimediality, and experiential learning and research by creatively expanding the networks of participation, the modes of access, and the tools for the creation and dissemination of scholarship. [1] The Graduate Portfolio in Digital Studies is a transcriptable credential in a cross-disciplinary academic area of inquiry that can be pursued by masters and doctoral students of any discipline at UT Austin. [1] The portfolio will be certified as an additional qualification together with the candidate's main degree at the end of their studies. [1]
MaxFails: Grades of C-, D, and F are not acceptable for graduate credit.

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Disability studies
Requirements: Successful applicants to the DS Master's Portfolio will have met the admission standards required by the Graduate School and by their primary Master's degree program. Students may enter the DS portfolio program at any point in their graduate work, but it is recommended that they do so as soon as they decide to pursue the portfolio. [4] The application should include: A statement of purpose, including previous experience related to individuals with disabilities, the relationship of DS to the student's program of studies, and relationship of DS to future career goals. [3, 4] Proof of enrollment and good academic standing in an approved graduate degree program. [3, 4] Consent from the student's Graduate Advisor or Dissertation Supervisor for participation in the DS portfolio area. [3, 4]
Department: UT School of Social Work, Texas Center for Disability Studies, School of Nursing, College of Education, College of Fine Arts, and College of Liberal Arts
Fees: For the academic year 2024-2025, the average graduate school tuition & fees are $12,006 for Texas residents and $22,954 for out-of-state students. [15]
CostPerCredit: The tuition per credit hour for part-time students is $659 for Texas residents and $1,245 for out-of-state students. [15]
ScholarshipType: Teaching and graduate research assistantships, Graduate Fellowships, Financial Aid. [19]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Dispute resolution
Requirements: Admission to the portfolio program is open to graduate students in good standing in approved degree programs at UT Austin. Students may apply at any stage of their graduate studies. Application materials include: A one-page essay explaining the relationship of dispute resolution to the student's degree program and career goals. Documentation of enrollment and good academic standing in a graduate program. A statement of support from the student's Graduate Advisor, Dissertation Supervisor, or equivalent faculty member. A proposed list of four courses (12 credit hours) with a written rationale for their inclusion. [4]
Department: School of Law and the Office of Graduate Studies
Description: The Graduate Portfolio Program in Dispute Resolution (GPP in DR) at The University of Texas at Austin is a cooperative initiative between the School of Law and the Office of Graduate Studies. The program brings together faculty and graduate students across disciplines—including law, public affairs, communication, architecture, engineering, business, nursing, social work, government, and sociology—to advance the study and practice of conflict and dispute resolution. [2, 3] The program is designed to integrate existing resources across the university into a structured framework that emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications. [2, 3] Students engage in coursework and research that address interpersonal, organizational, and societal conflict, while developing skills in mediation, negotiation, arbitration, and dispute systems design. [2] The objectives of the Graduate Portfolio Program are to: Encourage interdisciplinary research and dialogue among faculty and graduate students interested in dispute resolution. Provide a coherent plan of study that integrates theory, research, and practice. Equip students with analytical and methodological tools to examine and address conflict in diverse contexts. [2]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Energy studies
Requirements: Students in good standing in an approved graduate degree program may apply to the GPPES at any point in graduate study. [1] Candidates must complete and file a Portfolio Application Form with the GPPES Faculty Advisor. The application should include: A one-page essay describing the relationship of a specialization in energy to the student's degree program and career goals and interests; A list of the courses the student intends to use for the portfolio program. [1] The program requires twelve credit hours of coursework plus a 2-hour Energy Symposium. [3] One of the courses selected must be on energy-related environmental issues or energy law, and at least two courses must be from graduate programs other than the student's own major. [3]
Department: The Graduate Portfolio Program in Energy Studies is an interdisciplinary program and not housed in a single school or college.
Description: The Graduate Portfolio Program in Energy Studies (GPPES) takes an interdisciplinary approach designed to give students a broad picture of the energy field that considers energy issues from an overall policy perspective, based on an understanding of the technological and environmental pressures involved. [1] Completion of the GPPES is noted on the student's final transcript, providing future employers with an indication of the student's credentials in the field. [1] A core requirement of the GPPES is the gateway course, “Energy Technology and Policy,” jointly offered by a number of schools and colleges at UT, which focuses on the economic and environmental issues raised by both traditional and emerging energy technologies. [1] GPPES students also attend a weekly symposium in which distinguished speakers from UT and elsewhere discuss current concerns and recent developments in the energy field. [1] The GPPES is a cooperative effort involving eight schools and colleges of The University of Texas at Austin. [1] Students can design their own program to meet the coursework requirements of the GPPES by choosing from a wide range of courses offered by participating departments. [1] Participants in the program carry out an energy oriented research project – this can be a Master's thesis, a doctoral dissertation or a stand-alone project – and make a professional presentation of their results. [1] The program is managed by the Energy Institute. [1]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Ethical AI
Requirements: Students must submit the following three files when applying for admission to the Graduate Portfolio in Ethical AI: 1) Portfolio Application Form (name, EID, degree program, advisor, GPA, completed coursework with grades, plan of study for completing the Ethical AI Portfolio Program) 2) 250-500 word research statement 3) Approval Letter (or email) from Master's/PhD faculty research supervisor. [1]
Department: Interdisciplinary program connected to Good Systems and Texas Robotics
Description: The graduate portfolio program in Ethical AI is an interdisciplinary, socio-technical program for graduate students from all units across campus to anticipate and prepare for the complex interactions between AI-based technologies and society. [3, 4] Students will consider the ethical implications posed by AI-based technologies, as well as how innovation in AI is driven by societal forces. [3] They will gain experience in building human-centered AI systems as well as expertise in the ethical and societal dimensions of information technology. [3] Students will take four courses (at least two of them will be core Ethical AI courses) from at least two departments outside of their degree program. [3] They will then complete a research capstone experience resulting in a report, paper, thesis, or dissertation within the area of Ethical AI, which may include developing, designing, deploying, analyzing, and/or exploring the ethical and societal dimensions of AI-based technologies. [3] At the time of degree certification, students who complete all requirements for the portfolio program, as verified and approved by the steering committee, will receive a degree notation indicating that they have completed a Graduate Portfolio Program in Ethical AI on their final transcript. [3]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Food-Energy-Water-Systems (FEWS)
Requirements: The Graduate Portfolio in Food-Energy-Water-Systems is open to all University of Texas at Austin students currently enrolled in a master's or doctoral level degree in good standing in their departments. [1] Students must be in good academic standing and have permission of their graduate advisor to be considered for admission to the portfolio program. [1] Students interested in participating in the program must complete an online application form, which will include: Degree information, Faculty advisor name, Area of specialization and/or research focus, Proposed program of study in portfolio program (which courses the student intends to use for the portfolio program), a brief statement of the relationship of the portfolio program to degree program and professional goals, and signature of student and his/her faculty advisor. [1]
Department: The interdisciplinary Graduate Portfolio in Food-Energy-Water Systems includes courses from the Cockrell School of Engineering, the Jackson School of Geosciences, and the Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs. [9]
Description: A major challenge in Texas, the U.S, and the world is water scarcity and energy requirements for agriculture. Learn to develop new technologies, systems-level decision/management tools, and policies. [4] We are training future leaders at the food-energy-water-systems (FEWS) nexus to advance agriculture and food production in the U.S. and globally. [4] Graduate students will gain fundamental knowledge and tools needed to develop novel and sustainable solutions. [4]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Health communication
Requirements: The Graduate Portfolio in Health Communication is an option for current UT graduate students. Interested students should email the Center for Health Communication Director. [2]
Description: The Graduate Portfolio in Health Communication is offered by the Center for Health Communication. The portfolio is comprised of four graduate-level courses and allows students to develop an in-depth knowledge of the field of health communication including communication theory, research methods, and applications. These courses are taught by faculty in six departments across four schools, including the Moody College of Communication, and the Colleges of Education, Natural Sciences, and Nursing. [1]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Imaging science
Requirements: To be eligible to participate in a portfolio program, students must be admitted into one of the university's graduate degree programs. [7] Students not pursuing a BME or ECE graduate degree who are interested in completing the portfolio should apply by (a) submitting a brief statement of interest and their CV to the BME Graduate Coordinator and mia.markey@utexas.edu, and (b) by making an advising appointment. [6]
Concentration: ['Instrumentation, Devices, and Contrast Agents', 'Image processing', 'Modeling and visualization', 'Informatics']
Description: This program trains comprehensive imaging scientists in the skills necessary to improve the prevention, detection, diagnosis, and treatment of human diseases. The basic requirement to complete this portfolio program is 12 hours of coursework (4 courses), which provide the requisite core knowledge for an imaging scientist. [4]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Integrated behavioral health
Requirements: To be eligible to participate in a portfolio program, students must be admitted into one of the university's graduate degree programs. The requirements for participation include a minimum of 9 and a maximum of 15 credit hours of thematically related graduate coursework, with courses from at least two graduate programs outside of the student's primary degree major. [1] It also includes an independent paper or project or a scholarly essay presented at a research colloquium. [1] A portfolio program usually consists of four thematically related graduate courses and a scholarly paper or research presentation. [2]
Department: Graduate School (This is a cross-disciplinary portfolio program available to students enrolled in various graduate programs, including at the School of Nursing). [11, 9]
Fees: In-state: $12,006 - $13,784/Year, Out-of-state: $22,954 - $32,288/Year. [7, 2] Note: Portfolio programs do not have separate tuition; students pay the tuition associated with their primary graduate program. [9]
Description: Graduate portfolio programs provide opportunities for enrolled graduate students to obtain transcriptable credentials in cross-disciplinary academic areas of inquiry while they are completing the requirements for a master's or doctoral degree in a particular discipline. [3] Portfolio programs are intended to promote cross-disciplinary scholarship and study by bringing together faculty and students from a variety of disciplines whose interests transcend boundaries of traditional academic disciplines. [3] A portfolio program usually consists of four thematically related graduate courses and a scholarly paper or research presentation. [1] For master's portfolio students, a practical experience related to the portfolio program may be required in place of the paper/presentation. [1] The requirements include a minimum of 9 and a maximum of 15 credit hours of thematically related graduate coursework and an independent paper or project. [3]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships, fellowships, and assistantships are available. [11]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Integrated watershed studies
Requirements: To be eligible to participate in a portfolio program, students must be admitted into one of the university's graduate degree programs. [2] Graduate portfolio programs consist of a minimum of 9 and a maximum of 15 credit hours of thematically related graduate coursework. [2] Each student's portfolio must include content courses offered by at least two graduate programs outside of their primary degree major. [2] Upon completion, the student's University transcript reflects portfolio certification. [4]

ProgramName: Graduate Portfolio Program in Interdisciplinary European studies
Requirements: The application must be accompanied by the submission of a 1-2 pp. essay describing the importance of a particular interdisciplinary specialization or area study in European Studies to the student's doctoral program and career goals. [1]
Department: College of Liberal Arts, Center for European Studies
Description: The Doctoral Portfolio Program in Interdisciplinary European Studies enables students to establish strong interdisciplinary profiles based on focused cross-disciplinary coursework and research planning for studies of Europe. [1] It is open to all Ph. D. students on the UT-Austin campus and can be combined with programs such as social sciences, arts, communications, business and language studies. [1] The program aims to foster dialogue and communication among faculty and graduate students engaged in interdisciplinary European research, offer a venue for integrating perspectives from various disciplines, and promote high standards in interdisciplinary research. [1]
ScholarshipType: FLAS (Foreign Language and Area Studies) Fellowship

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Education
Requirements: All freshman applicants must submit the following: a completed Common App, a non-refundable application fee of $75, at least one essay and the required short answers, official SAT or ACT scores, and official high school transcripts. Applicants must also have completed or be on track to complete required high school coursework.
Concentration: ['Early Childhood through Grade Six ESL Generalist', 'Early Childhood through Grade Six ESL Bilingual Generalist', 'All-Level Generic Special Education', 'Youth and Community Studies']
Description: The College of Education offers four majors within the Bachelor of Science in Education degree. Through a unique combination of equity-minded coursework, students are guided by expert faculty and practitioners to manage, lead and teach in a variety of educational and community-based environments. Students who choose one of the Bachelor of Science in Education majors with a teacher preparation component are also on their way to teacher certification at any grade level. [5] The curriculum for the degree has the following components: University general education, major/focus area requirements, professional development sequence, and free electives. [4]
Accredidation: The University of Texas at Austin is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award baccalaureate, masters, professional, and doctorate degrees. [12, 15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Youth and Community Studies
Requirements: To complete a freshman application, applicants must submit an application form via the Common Application, pay a non-refundable $55 application fee (or receive a waiver), self-report their high school academic record using the Courses and Grades section of the Common App, and submit an ACT/SAT score. [4]
Concentration: ['Early Childhood', 'Special Populations', 'Coaching', 'Youth and Social Services', 'Physical Education Activity', 'UT Austin Urban Teachers English language arts and reading', 'UT Austin Urban Teachers social studies', 'Educational Leadership and Policy Studies (ELPS)']
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Education with a major in Youth and Community Studies prepares students to work with children, youth, and young adults in various settings that do not require teacher certification. [5] As a major, students undertake 24 hours of coursework focusing on individual differences, cultural and linguistic diversity, human learning in multicultural contexts, social concerns, theories of children's cognitive, social, and emotional development, the motivational value of play, and effective physical and health education, alongside educational leadership and social justice. [4, 6] The curriculum is composed of university general education, major requirements, a curricular specialization, a professional concentration, and free electives, totaling 120 semester credit hours. [7, 8] Career paths can include directing youth programs at various community-based agencies, parks and recreation departments, and educational programs sponsored by the government. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology and Health
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology and Health degree program requires a total of at least 120 semester hours of coursework. The curriculum includes the University-wide Core Curriculum, prescribed work for the Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology and Health, major requirements (which include a minor or specialization), and electives. [9] For all majors within this degree, a minimum of 36 hours must be in upper-division coursework. [9]
Concentration: ['applied movement science', 'exercise science', 'health promotion and behavioral science', 'physical culture and sports studies', 'sport management']
Description: The field of kinesiology consists of biomechanical, physiological, psychological, managerial, epidemiological, rehabilitative, and sociocultural approaches to the study of human movement and personal and public health. [1] The exercise science program is preparation for further study in sport and exercise sciences or in movement-related areas like physical therapy and sport medicine. [1] The health promotion and behavioral science major prepares graduates for professions in public health, community health promotion, and corporate wellness, among others. [1] The physical culture and sports studies major is for students preparing for graduate school or careers related to a social science approach to sport and exercise. [1] The sport management major is for those interested in the organization, marketing, and management of sport or entertainment programs. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Athletic Training
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Athletic Training is a competitive process that occurs after a student is admitted to the university. Students must apply to the Athletic Training Program (ATP). Requirements include a student's grade point average, completion of prescribed coursework, and participation in the Directed Observation Program. [6, 16] Applicants must also meet a set of technical standards, pass a health assessment/physical examination, provide proof of immunizations, and submit letters of recommendation and additional application documents. [6, 16] All interested students, including first-year and transfer students, must contact the program director, attend an orientation meeting, meet with an academic advisor, and complete prerequisite courses with a passing grade: KIN 312 Care and Prevention of Athletic Injuries, KIN 219K Introduction to Athletic Training, and CC 306M Introduction to Medical and Scientific Terminology. [19]
Description: In addition to completing the coursework associated with the athletic training major, students in the ATP must participate in clinical rotations and become adept in a set of educational competencies and clinical proficiencies. Students who plan to take the state licensure examination for athletic trainers must complete the ATP. The curriculum for the degree has four components: (a) the University-wide core curriculum; (b) prescribed work; (c) major requirements; and (d) electives.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Promotion and Behavioral Science
Requirements: Prospective University of Texas at Austin students should visit UT Admissions to learn about the application process. Freshman applications are reviewed holistically, considering class rank, strength of academic background, SAT/ACT scores, and an essay. [14, 5] For internal transfers into the Health Promotion and Behavioral Science major, students must have and maintain a minimum 2.5 GPA. [5]
Description: Our Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Health Promotion and Behavioral Science will prepare you to improve the health of individuals and communities. You’ll learn the science and art of health promotion through evidence-based practice and develop skills in planning, implementing, and evaluating health programs. With our focus on health equity, you’ll also understand how social determinants of health create health disparities and what we can do about it. As a graduate, you can work in a variety of settings, including nonprofit organizations, government agencies, schools, and health care.

Description: The objectives of the aerospace engineering degree program are to prepare students for professional practice in aerospace engineering and related engineering and scientific fields; to prepare students for such postbaccalaureate study as their aptitudes and professional goals may dictate; to instill in students a commitment to lifelong education and to ethical behavior throughout their professional careers; and to make students aware of the global and societal effects of technology. [5] The first two years of the aerospace engineering curriculum emphasize fundamental material along with engineering sciences, while the third year introduces concepts in the areas of aerodynamics and propulsion, structural mechanics, flight mechanics and orbital mechanics, and flight control. [5] The fourth year provides further depth in aerospace engineering, with emphasis on design and laboratory courses. [5] During the junior year, the student elects to pursue one of two design tracks, atmospheric flight or space flight. Description: Computational engineering is a relatively new field in engineering that recognizes the increasing demand for advanced computational methods in engineering practice. [1] It refers to the study and development of computer algorithms that translate mathematical and physical descriptions of engineering problems into languages and software that computers can process. [1] This emphasis distinguishes computational engineering from computer science and computer engineering. [1] The objectives of the computational engineering degree program are to prepare students for professional practice in engineering; to prepare students for such post-baccalaureate study as their aptitudes and professional goals may dictate; to instill in students a commitment to acquire and apply new knowledge and to ethical behavior throughout their professional careers; and to make students aware of the global and societal effects of technology. [1] The initial coursework in the computational engineering curriculum emphasize fundamental material along with engineering sciences, while the later coursework goes into further depth in mathematics, algorithms, computer languages, software engineering and design, and experimentation. [1] The major offers technical electives in the third and fourth years where students may choose from a variety of courses that orient them towards different engineering applications and better prepare those students who may choose to pursue a graduate degree. [3] Its field of practice covers the development, design, and control of processes and products that involve molecular change, both chemical and biological, and the operation of such processes. [3] Because many of the products that sustain and improve life are produced by carefully designed and controlled molecular changes, the chemical engineer serves in a wide variety of industries. [3] These industries range from chemical and energy companies to producers of all types of consumer and specialty products, pharmaceuticals, textiles, polymers, advanced materials, and solid-state and biomedical devices. [3] Careers are available in industry, government, consulting, and education. [3] Areas of professional work include research and development, operations, technical service, product development, process and plant design, market analysis and development, process control, and pollution abatement. ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Petroleum Engineering
Requirements: Applicants to the Cockrell School of Engineering must meet the calculus readiness requirement. This can be met by achieving a certain score on the SAT, ACT, or other calculus placement exams. All freshman applicants must submit an essay and the required short answer prompts as part of their application.
Description: The objective of the petroleum engineering program is to graduate practical, qualified engineers who can successfully pursue careers in the oil and gas production and services industries or similar areas. [3] Graduates of the program are expected to understand the fundamental principles of science and engineering behind the technology of petroleum engineering to keep their education current and to give them the capability of self-instruction after graduation. [3] They should be prepared to serve society by using the ideals of ethical behavior, professionalism, and environmentally responsible stewardship of natural resources. [3] Petroleum engineers are able to address and solve important technology challenges that will lead to energy security and societal prosperity, so the position is in high demand. [3] This challenging and rewarding field of engineering requires creative application of a wide spectrum of knowledge, including, but not limited to mathematics, physics, geology, and chemistry. [3] Worldwide energy demand is growing, and experts agree that oil and gas will continue to play an important role in the world's energy supply. [3] Petroleum engineers play a variety of roles within the energy business. [3] They design and monitor the drilling of exploratory and development wells used to locate and produce the oil and gas from the subsurface. [3] They work with technologies that can describe the characteristics of rocks deep beneath the surface and detect the type of fluids contained in those rocks. [3] They install and maintain the equipment that lifts fluids from subsurface reservoirs to the surface, and they design surface collection and treatment facilities to prepare produced hydrocarbons for delivery to a refinery or pipeline. [3] Hydraulic fracturing of shale gas and tight oil is the responsibility of a petroleum engineer, as is the development and implementation of enhanced oil recovery methods that capture stranded or bypassed hydrocarbons from old oilfields. [3] In addition to these traditional petroleum engineering career choices, there are other emerging careers for petroleum engineering graduates in pollution clean up, underground waste disposal (including the subsurface injection of carbon dioxide to reduce greenhouse gas emissions), and geothermal energy extraction. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geosystems Engineering

Description: Geosystems engineers are concerned with the development and use of engineering approaches in the management of natural resources from the earth's surface and subsurface. [2] This degree program, offered jointly by the Cockrell School of Engineering and the Jackson School of Geosciences, is designed to teach students the geological and engineering principles needed to solve subsurface resource development and environmental problems. [2] The curriculum includes a fundamental sequence of engineering and geological sciences courses in such areas as multiphase fluid flow, heat and mass transfer, field methods, and engineering design with applications to water and energy resources. [2] This interdisciplinary systems approach, combining engineering and geological sciences, is increasingly required to address complex real-world problems such as geothermal energy, the mining of strategic minerals, geologic storage of CO2 captured from the atmosphere, and pollution remediation and management of aquifers. [2] The degree program is designed to prepare graduates for successful careers with energy, environmental, and water resource management companies in addition to many government agencies. [2] Graduates of the program may pursue graduate study in environmental engineering, petroleum engineering, geology, and other related fields. [2] Graduates are expected to understand the fundamental principles of science and engineering behind subsurface processes involved in energy and water resources to keep their education from becoming outdated and to give them the capability of self-instruction after graduation. [2] They should also be prepared to serve society by applying the ideals of ethical behavior, professionalism, and environmentally responsible stewardship of natural resources. [2]

[3] The program maintains a balance and integration among the four sub-fields: Biological, Cultural, Linguistic, and Archaeological. The curriculum combines core HDO courses and a variety of approved courses from other departments. [4, 6]

The study of linguistics can prepare students to teach a foreign language, become a speech therapist, work in the field of computer science and artificial intelligence, or work with native peoples or with immigrant groups. As with all liberal arts degrees, the analytical skills used in the study of linguistics will prepare students to problem solve and to think critically in a wide range of career choices. For those students interested in graduate school, the linguistics program here at the University of Texas offers a variety of research opportunities. Working closely with professors and graduate students will give students the experience they need to prepare for graduate programs.

Description: The B.S. in Human Development and Family Sciences focuses on the study of human development, individuals in a family context, relationships, and well-being within the family and the broader social, economic, community, and governmental environment. [5, 13] Students in the program are expected to develop knowledge and understanding about human development and family dynamics through classroom experiences, observation of children and families, and research. [5, 13] They have opportunities to apply their knowledge through practicum experiences in research and placements in the field. [5, 13] The program is designed to give students excellent preparation for graduate training that leads to careers in academia, research, medicine, and other health professions, as well as for employment in a field involving work with children, families, and adults. [5, 13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Apparel and Textiles
Requirements: Required for ALL freshman applicants who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or who are graduating from a Texas high school: Apply using the Common App, pay the non-refundable application fee of $75, submit at least one essay and the required short answer prompts, submit SAT and ACT official test scores, and provide high school transcripts.
Concentration: ['Design', 'Merchandising', 'Textiles']
Description: The Division of Textiles and Apparel (TXA) is a science-based interdisciplinary hub providing a dynamic education – setting students up for a breadth of career and academic opportunities. Students in the Division of Textiles and Apparel are able to select from a wide range of innovative courses on campus, in New York City, NY, or Paris, France, or in studios and labs in collaboration with industry partners in the Austin, TX area. [1] TXA students study the art of design, the science of chemistry and physics, and the application of retail principles. [1, 5] Students complete a major foundation curriculum and then choose from courses which will make up Specializations– with students tracking through introductory, developing, and mastery learning levels of content. [1] Our courses provide hands-on experience reflective of a rapidly evolving field – harnessing the energy of rapidly evolving retail environments, learning from intercultural practices and customs, product development, consumer behavior, apparel and fashion design, computer-aided design, sustainability, and fiber and fabric testing, among other things. Description: The English major at UT offers a first-rate education. Our students graduate with a thorough grounding in British, American, and world literature written in English and its cultural and historical contexts, yet our degree plan is flexible enough to allow students to concentrate in other areas of particular interest, such as creative writing or cultural studies. Just as importantly, English majors learn to articulate and defend their ideas, to turn research and critical thinking into cogent arguments, and to express themselves clearly and with style.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Writing
Requirements: To apply for freshman admission to the University of Texas at Austin, all applicants must submit a completed application, a non-refundable application fee of $75 (or a fee waiver), at least one essay and the required short answer prompts, and official high school transcripts. For the 2025-2026 application cycle, official SAT or ACT scores are also required. An expanded resume is an optional item that can be submitted to provide more information about activities and achievements.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Rhetoric and Writing major aims to produce sophisticated communicators able to perform the sort of analyses and persuasive presentations that such careers require. Analytical, Communicative, and Persuasive skills are in high demand in almost every profession, including law, education, politics, consulting, business, public relations, professional writing, advertising, and academia. As a Rhetoric & Writing major, you will develop your ability to apply these practical skills in person, in print, and electronically, while studying the rhetorical and philosophical principles in which they are based. It is also an excellent preparation for graduate-level study in law, business, media studies, literary and cultural studies, and other liberal-arts disciplines. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts and Sciences/Liberal Studies
Requirements: Required application materials for all freshman applicants include the Common App, a non-refundable application fee of $75, an essay, and short answers. [12] Applicants must also submit an official high school transcript showing their class rank. [9]
Description: The requirements for the Bachelor of Arts under Plan I are designed to give each student flexibility in the selection of courses to meet individual needs. A total of 120 semester hours is required. Thirty-nine hours must be in upper-division courses. At least 60 hours, including 24 hours of upper-division coursework, must be completed in residence at the University. Provided residence rules are met, credit may be earned by examination, by extension, by correspondence (up to 30 percent of the hours required for the degree), or, with the approval of the dean, by work transferred from another institution. Up to 16 semester hours of classroom and/or correspondence coursework may be taken on the pass/fail basis; this coursework may be counted only as electives.† The specific requirements for the Bachelor of Arts, Plan I, consist of prescribed work, major and minor requirements, and electives.
Accredidation: The University of Texas at Austin is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award baccalaureate, masters, professional and doctorate degrees.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Humanities/Humanistic Studies
Requirements: Required application materials for freshman admission include: the Common App, a non-refundable application fee of $75, at least one essay and the required short answer prompts, official high school transcripts showing class rank, and SAT or ACT official test scores. [15] An expanded resume and up to two letters of recommendation are optional. The Humanities program is a self-designed major within the College of Liberal Arts that students create after being admitted to the university in consultation with a program advisor. [8, 13]
Description: The Humanities Program offers highly motivated students the opportunity to design their own course of study as a major for the B.A. degree. [4] Due to the flexibility of this major, students study a wide range of topics that go beyond traditional disciplines associated with Humanities, such as arts and literature. [4] While Liberal Arts classes provide the foundation for the Humanities major, many students integrate courses from other colleges. [4] Recent Humanities contracts have included topics such as “Women's Roles in Globalized Medicine”, “Human Rights”, “Children's Visual Media”, and “Game Theory”. [4] As honors students, Humanities majors are engaged in research. [4] This unique major culminates in a required honors thesis written during the senior year. [4] The thesis allows students to design a project, conduct in-depth research, and work closely with a faculty supervisor. [4]
